strengths: Novel and well-motivated approach using compressed KV-cache as supervision signal for latent reasoning, addressing a real limitation of prior work
Technically sound execution combining redundancy-aware KV eviction with KV-matching loss and complementary CODI distillation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model scales (0.5B-3B) and families with both in-distribution and OOD testing
Consistent improvements across all tested settings with particularly strong gains on natural language reasoning traces where prior methods struggle
Significant efficiency improvements (62-92% fewer forward passes) while maintaining reasoning performance
Thorough ablation studies examining components, loss types, eviction methods, and architectural choices
Strong interpretability analysis including decoded latent traces and detailed KV-cache correspondence visualization
Well-structured presentation with clear motivation and compelling figures
weaknesses: Evaluation severely limited to GSM8k math word problems only; no testing on other reasoning domains (logical, commonsense, code) raises serious generalization concerns

Significant hyperparameter sensitivity with different values required per model/dataset (λ∈{0,0.1}, loss type varies, projection layer sometimes disabled), suggesting domain-specific tuning rather than robust generalization
Limited theoretical understanding of why KV-matching works better than alternatives; lacks principled explanation for design choices

Critical technical ambiguity: importance score computation uses answer tokens during training but unclear how compression is determined at test time for new questions without known answers, creating potential train-test mismatch
Training overhead not discussed despite requiring both teacher and student KV-cache computation; only inference efficiency reported
Interpretability claims don't fully hold: decoded latent traces are often uninterpretable, particularly for natural language training (Section 5.1), contradicting motivation
Individual components not novel (R-KV, CODI, Jacobi iterations from prior work); main novelty is combination plus KV-matching loss
Choice of M=24 latent tokens appears arbitrary with limited parametric study; no systematic investigation of sensitivity to this key choice
Some experimental comparisons use results copied from other papers (marked †) rather than direct head-to-head evaluation on same hardware
